story:
In the beginning, a creator couple had four sons: the smallest was a war and sun deity, and his brothers were named Precious Serpent, Our Lord Flayed, and Smoking Mirror. The parents ordered the smallest son and Precious Serpent to bring order to the world. Together they made fire, the first man and woman, the Earth, and the Sun.

In another telling, a fierce goddess was sweeping atop a sacred mountain when a ball of feathers fell and impregnated her. Her other children, four hundred sons and a daughter, were enraged at this and conspired to kill her. As they attacked, the youngest son burst from her womb fully armed and grown. He fought his brothers and beheaded his sister, casting her body down the mountain, then chased his brothers until they scattered across the sky as stars. He became the sun, his sister the moon, and his brothers the stars, and ever after the sun chases the moon and stars.

Later, this god led his people from their original home, ordering them to abandon it and take a new name. He left them briefly under his sister's rule; she founded a settlement, but the people resented her, so he put her to sleep and had the people leave without her. She awoke, enraged, and bore a son who later confronted the god and was killed by him; the god tore out his heart and threw it into a lake. He then commanded his people to find that heart and build their city where they saw an eagle on a cactus eating a serpent. They found this sign on a lake island and founded their city there.
